note: Part 2 mid-demo at verify.sh's cycle counts (PAL 32,000,000, NTSC 28,000,000): different frames on the two models, so every check is per model and there is no PAL-vs-NTSC 'same' strip. Written by plan/pin-p2-demo.py (a builder's script, not in the public tree) from the part's tables at the state read off the shots: PAL: rows 0 to 13 at offset 5, rows 14 to 24 at offset 4, bar position 5, band line 1 phase 9 (ink cyan), band line 100 phase 43 (ink light green); NTSC: rows 0 to 14 at offset 4, rows 15 to 24 at offset 3, bar position 11, band line 0 phase 52 (ink light blue), band line 100 phase 25 (ink cyan). Ink ink_tab[(row - offset) & 15], paper pap_line[((row + offset) & 15) + column / 4], bar bar_tab[(entry - position) & 15]; twister edges from the recipe's phase script. An exit shot is torn at the beam's line and the roll writes two rows a frame top to bottom, so each row's offset is read for itself and the bar position from the entries above the tear. Re-pin whenever the timeline moves (music or sync positions).
